details: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has proposed a new framework for crypto assets, introducing two exemptions from the registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933. The first allows firms to issue up to $5 million in crypto tokens over four years, while the second permits offerings up to $75 million every 12 months.

title: US SEC Proposes New Crypto Asset Framework

details: UK challenger Revolut has introduced EURR, an Ethereum-based, euro-denominated digital token. This marks the initial phase of its stablecoin strategy, with a phased rollout commencing for eligible customers in Denmark, Poland, and Portugal, and wider availability expected in other EEA markets later this year.

title: Revolut Launches Euro-Backed Stablecoin EURR

details: Bitcoin crossed the $80,000 mark for the first time in approximately three months, capping a 25 percent rally since August 19. This surge was fueled by significant inflows into U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds, which recorded $1.9 billion in net inflows last week, marking the strongest weekly tally since October 2025. On August 28, US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $242 million in inflows, marking their ninth consecutive day of positive net flows.

title: Bitcoin Surges Past $80,000 Amid Strong ETF Inflows

details: The U.S. Treasury's recent decision to at least double the size of its debt buyback purchases to $4 billion per operation sparked a Bitcoin short squeeze. This event led to a record $3.1 billion in crypto short positions being wiped out over two days. Some analysts suggest this intervention amounted to a form of yield curve control.

title: US Treasury Debt Buybacks Spark Bitcoin Short Squeeze

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) issued a warning in July 2026, stating that disruptions in blockchain systems could spread more rapidly than institutions are capable of responding. The European Central Bank (ECB) also noted that the automated nature of tokens could amplify the risk of problems cascading across different platforms.

title: IMF Warns of Risks from Blockchain System Disruptions

details: Major U.S. banks and stock exchanges are significantly increasing their investments in blockchain projects, aiming to accelerate financial market settlements and reduce transaction costs through tokenization. This involves converting traditional assets like cash, stocks, and bonds into digital form on the blockchain for 24/7 trading, with the total value of stablecoins already exceeding $300 billion worldwide.
